newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cardoso will ensure Brazil civil service bill vote.
newsitem.headline: Cardoso will ensure Brazil civil service bill vote.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso will intervene personally to make sure the Chamber of Deputies votes on the government's civil service reform bill in the first week of April, a spokesman said.
"If it takes meetings between the president and deputies, then there will be meetings," said spokesman Sergio Amaral.
The government had hoped to put its civil service reform to a first of two votes in the lower house Wednesday.
But the vote was called off after whips failed to overcome resistance from a number of deputies who stand to lose out under a proposed public sector pay ceiling included in the bill.
Amaral said the president had given his "total support" to the text of the reform and would "personally get involved" to make sure it was put a vote in the Chamber of Deputies April 2.

The civil service reform seeks to reduce public spending by allowing states and municipalities to cut staff and by putting a 10,800 real ($10,285) ceiling on pay and benefits for public sector workers and pensioners.

Newspapers say the ceiling would hit the incomes of 140 members of the 513-strong Chamber of Deputies, making it hard for the government to get the two three-fifths majorities needed for approval of the constitutional amendment in the lower house.
